1) the amino acid at position 1388 of the sulfonyl urea receptor 1 subunit is crucial for the trafficking of ATP-sensitive potassium channels to the plasma membrane, 2) the amino acid side-chain at this position is also critical for the proper function of the channel, and 3) the F1388L mutation in the SUR subunit generates a novel channel phenotype with increased sensitivity to metabolic inhibition and diazoxide.

the amino acid residue Phe-138 in the sulfonylueurea receptor is required for proper trafficking and function in ATP-sensitive potassium channels and that the residue can be replaced with leucine to generate a channel variant that is sensitive to diazoxide and both pinacidil and glibenclamid.
a single amino acid in the SUR1 subunit of KATP channel controls trafficking efficiency and channel function.
